title: Invariant anticanonical indices and conversion of twisted differentials
main_claim: Thm 1.1: for a compact torus acting holomorphically on a compact complex manifold, with -K_F naturally linearized, the invariant index I_T(m) equals a polynomial P on multiples of some a>0, and P(0)=I_T(0). Thm 1.2: if S is smooth projective, -K_S is smoothly semipositive and D is pseudoeffective with H^0(m_j L - D) nonzero for unbounded m_j, then some kL is effective. Application (Cor 5.2): if -K_X is smoothly semipositive then -mK_X is effective for some m>0, obtained by descending invariant twisted forms to a finite cover and then converting.

issues.location: Thm 4.1 / Lemma 4.2 (LMPTX [14, Thm 4.1]) and Section 5 (companion [18] finite-cover theorem)
issues.description: Two steps are external black boxes. (1) The pseudoeffectivity of -M for a saturated rank-one subsheaf of (Omega^1)^{⊗b} is taken from LMPTX Thm 4.1 in its smooth, zero-boundary case. (2) The finite cover whose universal cover is C^q x C x F, with monodromy on F through a compact torus T, invariant canonical frames, and F having no holomorphic forms of positive degree, is taken from the companion paper [18]. The anticanonical nonvanishing corollary rests on both. Neither was checked here.
issues.evidence: Section 4: 'This is the smooth, zero-boundary, rank-one case of [14, Theorem 4.1]'. Section 5: 'We use the following finite-cover structure statement from [18, ...]'.

coverage: Read the whole paper from the PDF; the LaTeX section files are missing from build/source. Theorem 1.1: checked the Lefschetz denominator expansions and their signs, testing the convention on P^1 with O(2) and getting the character t+1+t^{-1}. Checked that -w = sum alpha_i u_i, so u lies in the affine span of D; the binomial identity (2.1), including validity for m<h and the value at m=0; the deformation retraction in Lemma 2.2; the inclusion-exclusion/nerve step giving chi(D)-chi(A)=0; and agreement with the actual m=0 contributions (only components with I empty contribute). Theorem 1.2: checked the maximality property (pencil plus joint map), the class identity (3.3) and the affine formula for horizontal coefficients, the Hilbert-flattening dimension count, the b_P normalization and that sigma is regular, rank one of G_k for every k>=0 including k=0, the adjoint identity (3.9), the Berndtsson moments, the Hölder/Dini limit, the lower bound from properness, the upper bound at general points of each boundary divisor, the extensions across divisors and across codimension two, the Skoda/Demailly-Kollár construction of a metric with trivial multiplier ideal, the hypotheses of Fujino's Kollár-Nadel theorem, Q(0)=h^0(f_*O(E))>0, and the pushforward pi_*O(E)=O_S. Lemma 4.2: checked the generic-span wedge, saturation, and the direct-summand argument. Also checked Cor 2.5 (equivariant hard Lefschetz with averaging), the descent in Prop 5.1, and the finite étale norm step.
sibling_notes: This is consistent with the family-068 siblings (ranks 6, 22, 89, 218, 229), which all returned no_gap_found and flagged the same kind of black-box dependence on LMPTX Thm 4.1 and on companion finite-cover/torus-monodromy results. This paper's Theorem 1.2 argument (maximal dominated base, rank-one adjoint direct images, Berndtsson metric, vanishing at k=0) follows the same pattern siblings verified in the Cohomological-transfer and Integrable-metrics papers.
